newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- DRINKS GROUPS IN 24 BILLION STG MERGER

Drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan have announced plans to merge. The proposed alliance would create the world's largest spirits and wines group, with a likely value of 23.8 billion stg. News of the plans prompted industry rivals Seagram to threaten to oppose the merger in representations to competition authorities around the globe.
-- UK SET TO MEET INFLATION TARGET, SAYS GEORGE

Eddie George, the governor of the Bank of England, has forecast that the UK has a 'better or even chance' of meeting the government's inflation target. George also said he expected inflation to decline in coming months. The comments, made in Switzerland where George was meeting with central bankers from the Group of 10 leading industrial countries, come ahead of the publication of the Bank's quarterly Inflation Report on Tuesday.
-- BRUSSELS BACKS AWAY FROM CLASH ON LABOUR'S VAT CUT

Chancellor Gordon Brown has secured the new government's first concession from Brussels after European Commission backed away from its opposition to British plans to cut VAT on fuel from 8 to 5 per cent. The reduction is expected to be announced in Brown's summer budget, due in June or July. While the Commission is opposed in principle to cuts in VAT, Mario Monti, single market commissioner, said he did 'not see any particular obstacle at this stage' to the one-off reduction.
-- FINANCE MINISTERS WARN ITALY ON EMU

European Union finance ministers have issued a sharp warning to Italy over its preparations to meet the criteria for joining monetary union. At a meeting in Brussels, the ministers said the Italian government needed to take more steps to meet the Maastricht deficit target of 3 per cent of gross domestic product in 1997 and beyond.
-- COMPANY TREASURERS UNPREPARED FOR EMU

Research from US-based banking industry consultancy Greenwich Associates has found that many corporate treasurers are still not preparing for the impact of European monetary union on their financial arrangements. The study found that only 64 per cent of corporate treasury departments in continental Europe said they were actively preparing for EMU. In the UK, the figure was just 41 per cent.
-- LATE PAYMENT BILL ADDED TO POLICY LIST

The government is preparing proposals for statutory interest on late payment of bills. The measures, a demonstration of the government's commitment to helping small businesses, is the latest addition to the list of 22 pieces of legislation due in Wednesday's Queen's Speech. The government itself, as well as all other public sectors, will also be subject to the provisions.
-- CHINA MAY SEEK GREATER STAKE IN HK TELECOM

According to the Chairman of Citic, the Chinese company which recently sold its 7.7 per cent stake in Hongkong Telecom, China may be looking to acquire a bigger stake in the telecoms monopoly. The chairman, Larry Juang, said that any deal would have to be done on commercial terms and it would be very difficult to persuade Cable & Wireless, who currently hold a 59 per cent stake in HkT, to sell. Juang added HKT would benefit from closer ties with mainland operators.
-- BRITISH BIOTECH SET FOR FIRST DRUG LAUNCH

British Biotech, the largest UK biotechnology company, continues to make progress towards the commercialisation of its first product, Zacutex, a drug for acute pancreatitis. Clinical trials and senior marketing appointments are continuing for the product which is establishing sales subsidiaries in the UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Nordic region and Spain.
-- BIOTECH TRUST TO RAISE UP TO 25 MILLION STG

Investment fund group International Biotechnology Trust has made plans to raise up to 25 million stg through the placing and offer of C shares. Trust's central area of business is mid-stage investment to help biotechnology companies through the transition from venture capital backing to a stock market listing. The company is currently planning an increase of investment in countries such as France, Germany and the UK.
-- SALES ABROAD BOOST TELEFONICA

Spanish telecoms company Telefonica released its first quarter figures on Monday, which included net attributable profits up 15.7 per cent to $194 million and consolidated revenues up 20.8 per cent from the same period in 1996. The group attributed much of its success to its international division and operators such as Tisa in Latin America. Growth in the Latin American market is encouraging for the new BT/MCI merger, as they plan to move into the area with the aid of partner Telefonica.
